intent_en: To demonstrate how different policy scenarios, ranging from free market approaches to direct government mandates, influence the speed of market adoption for electric machines over time.
previous_intent: To illustrate the range of modeled scenarios for transitioning from fossil fuel-based machines to electric ones, ranging from market-driven approaches to rapid direct replacement.
narration_support: Sol's research modeled different scenarios for the transition from fossil fuel -based machines to electric ones, from a market -driven transition to carbon taxes, to a much more direct and heavy -handed approach that would replace our machines with their electric counterparts very quickly.
chart_support: Line chart plotting market adoption against time for various scenarios (free market, carbon tax, direct replacement), showing that direct intervention scenarios achieve full adoption much faster than market-driven ones.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly describes modeling different transition scenarios from market-driven to direct replacement, and the chart visualizes these specific scenarios (Free market, Low/High carbon tax, Early retirement/100% replacement) showing their impact on adoption speed over time.
